**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Stem at a branch node/junction
- **Key features**:
  - Elongated, cracked stem lesion with dark brown to reddish-brown necrotic tissue in the center
  - Lighter/bleached tissue surrounding the dark brown core
  - Stem appears to have split open, revealing discolored vascular/pith tissue inside
  - No fungal structures (no spore masses, no sclerotia, no white mycelium)
  - Still-green stem tissue adjacent to the canker

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato**: "brown canker lesions on stems" with vascular involvement — the cracked, elongated stem lesion with internal brown discoloration fits well. No fungal signs are expected.
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: Stem cankers "near the soil line" with "concentric rings" and cracked/dry pith — the cracking fits, but concentric rings are not visible, and this appears higher on the plant.
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: Requires white cottony mycelium — absent here.
- **Southern_Blight**: Requires white mycelium and sclerotia at soil line — absent here.

The elongated, cracked stem canker with dark brown internal discoloration at a node, no fungal structures, on an upper stem area most closely matches **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato**.
